From f27cfdcfc916bb59297825805f4c3499f89f9e76 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dikshita Agarwal <dikshita.agarwal@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 12:37:42 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] media: iris: Fix use-after-free in
 iris_release_internal_buffers()

The recent change in commit 1dabf00ee206 ("media: iris: gen1: Destroy
internal buffers after FW releases") introduced a regression where
session_release_buf() may free the buffer. The caller,
iris_release_internal_buffers(), continued to access `buffer` after the
call, leading to a potential use-after-free.

Fix this by setting BUF_ATTR_PENDING_RELEASE before calling
session_release_buf(), and reverting the flag if the call fails. This
ensures no dereference occurs after potential freeing.

Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/aYXvKAX3Pg3sL37P@stanley.mountain/#r
Signed-off-by: Dikshita Agarwal <dikshita.agarwal@oss.qualcomm.com>
Reviewed-by: Vikash Garodia <vikash.garodia@oss.qualcomm.com>
Fixes: 1dabf00ee206 ("media: iris: gen1: Destroy internal buffers after FW releases")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Bryan O'Donoghue <bod@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil+cisco@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_buffer.c b/drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_buffer.c
index 9151f43bc6b9..1d53c7414b75 100644
--- a/drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_buffer.c
+++ b/drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_buffer.c
@@ -582,10 +582,12 @@ static int iris_release_internal_buffers(struct iris_inst *inst,
 			continue;
 		if (!(buffer->attr & BUF_ATTR_QUEUED))
 			continue;
+		buffer->attr |= BUF_ATTR_PENDING_RELEASE;
 		ret = hfi_ops->session_release_buf(inst, buffer);
-		if (ret)
+		if (ret) {
+			buffer->attr &= ~BUF_ATTR_PENDING_RELEASE;
 			return ret;
-		buffer->attr |= BUF_ATTR_PENDING_RELEASE;
+		}
 	}
 
 	return 0;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

The patch fixes a use-after-free bug in `iris_release_internal_buffers()` caused by accessing a buffer after it might have been freed by `session_release_buf()`.

### Modifications in `drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_buffer.c`

- **Before the fix**: The code called `session_release_buf()` and then, on success, set the `BUF_ATTR_PENDING_RELEASE` flag on the buffer. This was problematic because `session_release_buf()` could free the buffer, leading to a use-after-free when setting the flag.
- **After the fix**: The `BUF_ATTR_PENDING_RELEASE` flag is set **before** calling `session_release_buf()`. If the call fails, the flag is cleared. This ensures no buffer access occurs after it might have been freed.

### Relationship (single file)

Since the entire change is confined to one file, there is no cross-file relationship. The fix reorders the operations within the same loop to eliminate the dangerous access after a free, and adds proper error handling to revert the flag on failure.
